beats.beat: The company's product range spans Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM) and Hard Minerals (HM) — inputs for a variety of industrial applications.
It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network, making the promoter a critical business partner.

The company lists six competitive strengths: a diversified product portfolio, diverse user industries, import substitution potential, support from the holding company, product innovation through continuous R&D, and a strong management team.
Customer concentration is high — the top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017.
Exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka have totalled Rs 1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

beats.beat: The company turned profitable from FY2015 after two years of losses: PAT (Rs lakh) was -27.40 in FY2013, -12.17 in FY2014, then 149.58 in FY2015, 90.18 in FY2016, 174.82 in FY2017, and 132.75 in H1 FY2018 (six months ended September 2017).
Cash flow from operations has been volatile: (Rs lakh) 200.97 in FY2013, 127.73 in FY2014, 422.36 in FY2015, 802.59 in FY2016, negative 349.75 in FY2017, and 124.86 in H1 FY2018.
Total assets have grown overall: Rs 3,018.66 lakh in FY2013, 2,679.38 in FY2014, 2,592.53 in FY2015, 2,767.21 in FY2016, 3,273.96 in FY2017, and 3,424.96 in H1 FY2018.
Basic earnings per share (EPS in Rs) improved from negative in FY2013 (-0.45) and FY2014 (-0.20) to positive thereafter: 2.47 in FY2015, 1.46 in FY2016, 2.43 in FY2017, and 1.48 in H1 FY2018.
The company acknowledges negative cash flows in certain prior years as a risk factor, noting that sustained negative cash flow could impact growth and business.

beats.beat: The promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited. They collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital.
The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds an additional 21,510 shares — just 0.24% of pre-issue capital — meaning non-promoter public holding is negligible before the issue.
The company has entered into related party transactions, as per Accounting Standard 18, details of which are referenced to page 223 of the DRHP.

Governance flags include: the company does not own the premises for two manufacturing facilities and its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur; there have been instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the ROC; and certain statutory licenses for its Plot 9-10 facility in GIDC Waghodia have not yet been obtained.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals segment was estimated at Rs 1,000 billion in FY2017, part of a broader chemicals industry (ex-pharma and fertilisers) of Rs 5,800–6,200 billion.
The segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017 and is forecast to grow at 12–14% CAGR, according to CRISIL Research.
Within specialty chemicals, construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients are each expected to grow at 15% CAGR; polymer additives at 10%; and others at 12–13%.
The industry is highly fragmented, with small and medium enterprises holding 70–75% market share, but a few Indian players have the scale to compete globally.

Key demand drivers include rising consumption, urbanisation, government initiatives (Draft National Chemical Policy, 100% FDI, PCPIRs), and shifting global supply from China due to stricter environmental norms.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals — Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals — and relies on its corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited to market and sell its products.

The company is raising capital through a public issue on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and for general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who 20 Microns Nano Minerals is, what it does, and that it is raising equity to fund a new facility and list on the SME board.

beats.beat: The issue is managed by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited as the lead manager; Link Intime India Private Limited is the registrar.
Proceeds will fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and also be used for general corporate purposes.
The issue also aims to create a public trading market for the company's shares by listing on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE), enhancing visibility and brand.

The DRHP does not disclose whether the offer includes a fresh issue component, an offer for sale, or the identity of any selling shareholder — these details are not specified in the available excerpts.

beats.beat: No long-term agreements: The company operates without long-term contracts with either customers or raw material suppliers, relying instead on purchase orders. This exposes it to sudden volume or price changes.
Negative operating cash flow: In FY2017, cash flow from operations was negative (Rs -349.75 lakh), and the company itself cites this as a risk that could affect growth and financial stability.
Unlicensed facility: The manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, has not yet obtained certain required statutory and regulatory approvals, creating potential liability if penalised.
Contingent liabilities: As of September 30, 2017, the company had contingent liabilities and commitments aggregating to Rs 29.11 lakh, which could materialise and impact profitability.
